name: LM2904DR2G
title: Single-supply dual operational amplifiers (LM258, LM358, LM358A, LM358E, LM2904, LM2904A, LM2904E, LM2904V, NCV2904)
summary: A family of dual general-purpose bipolar op amps, internally compensated, that work from one supply of 3.0 V to 32 V or from split supplies up to ±16 V. The input range and the output swing both include the negative rail, and supply current is 0.7 mA for both amplifiers at 5 V. Grades differ in temperature range (0 to +70°C up to -40 to +125°C) and in offset and bias limits; the LM2904DR2G is the -40 to +105°C grade in SOIC-8 on reels of 2500.

circuits.title: Voltage reference
circuits.description: An MC1403 2.5 V reference drives the non-inverting input of one amplifier. R1 from the output to the inverting input and R2 from there to ground set a non-inverting gain, so the output is 2.5 V times (1 + R1/R2).

circuits.title: Wien bridge oscillator
circuits.description: A sine oscillator on one amplifier, run from a single supply with Vref at half of VCC. The positive feedback path is a series R and C from the output to the non-inverting input, with a parallel R and C from that input to Vref; it sets the frequency at 1/(2πRC), 1.0 kHz with R = 16 kΩ and C = 0.01 µF. The negative feedback is 10 kΩ from Vref to the inverting input and 50 kΩ back from the output, shunted by a 5.0 kΩ potentiometer, its wiper tied to one end, in series with two diodes in inverse parallel.

parts.note: potentiometer, wiper tied to one end

notes: Vref = VCC/2.

circuits.title: High impedance differential amplifier
circuits.description: Three amplifiers make a differential amplifier whose inputs both see a non-inverting input. Amplifiers A1 and A2 each take one input; R1 between their inverting inputs, with aR1 and bR1 as their feedback resistors, sets the first-stage gain. A third amplifier takes the difference of the two outputs through R/C input resistors and R feedback and ground resistors, giving eo = C(1 + a + b)(e2 - e1).
notes: Resistor values are symbolic: a, b and C are ratios chosen by the designer.

circuits.title: Comparator with hysteresis
circuits.description: One amplifier used as a comparator. The signal goes to the inverting input; Vref reaches the non-inverting input through R1, and R2 from the output back to that input adds positive feedback. The output switches at VinH going up and VinL going down; the band between them is R1/(R1 + R2) times the output swing.

circuits.title: Bi-quad filter
circuits.description: Four amplifiers in a state-variable bi-quad with a bandpass output and a notch output, biased at Vref = VCC/2. A1 is a summing stage with a parallel R and C in its feedback; A2 is an integrator (R in, C feedback); A3 is a unity-gain inverter (100 kΩ in and feedback) whose output returns to A1's input through R. The bandpass output is taken at A1. A4 sums the input (through R2) and the bandpass signal (through R1) with R3 feedback, and C1 couples the notch output. With R = 160 kΩ, C = 0.001 µF and R1 = R2 = R3 = 1.6 MΩ, the centre frequency is 1.0 kHz, Q = 10, and both gains are 1.

parts.note: R, A3 output back to A1 input

notes: Vref = VCC/2. TBP is the gain at the centre frequency, TN the passband gain of the notch output.

circuits.title: Function generator
circuits.description: Two amplifiers make a triangle and square wave generator, biased at Vref = VCC/2. A1 is an integrator: Rf from the square output into its inverting input, C as feedback, Vref on its non-inverting input; its output is the triangle wave. A2 is a comparator with hysteresis: the triangle reaches its non-inverting input through R3 (75 kΩ), R1 (100 kΩ) ties that input to Vref and R2 (300 kΩ) feeds back from the output; its inverting input sits at Vref. Its output is the square wave.
notes: R3 = R1·R2/(R1 + R2): 75 kΩ is 100 kΩ in parallel with 300 kΩ.

circuits.title: Multiple feedback bandpass filter
circuits.description: A single-amplifier multiple feedback bandpass filter biased at Vref = VCC/2. The input goes through R1 to a node with R2 to ground; from that node one C goes to the output and another C to the inverting input, and R3 runs from the output to the inverting input. CO, ten times C, couples the output. R1, R2 and R3 follow from the chosen centre frequency, C, Q and centre gain.
notes: A voltage follower ahead of the filter holds its response steady where the source impedance changes.

where.R: the two equal bridge resistors, 16 kΩ for 1.0 kHz
where.C: the two equal bridge capacitors, 0.01 µF for 1.0 kHz

where.a: ratio of A1's feedback resistor to R1
where.b: ratio of A2's feedback resistor to R1
where.C: ratio of the output stage's feedback R to its input R/C

operation.text: Each device holds two independent, internally compensated amplifiers sharing supply pins; the pair is half of an LM324 quad. Per amplifier the supply current is roughly a fifth of an MC1741's. The grades differ in temperature range and in offset, bias and gain limits: LM358 0 to +70°C, LM258 -25 to +85°C, LM2904 -40 to +105°C, LM2904V and NCV2904 -40 to +125°C. NCV parts are AEC-Q100 qualified and PPAP capable, for automotive use with site and change control.
A single supply runs from 3.0 V to VCC(max) with VEE/Gnd at ground. Split supplies run from ±1.5 V to the maximum on each rail.

The common mode range reaches down to the negative supply (ground on one supply), which in many applications removes the need for external biasing parts. The top of the range is VCC - 1.7 V. Neither input may go more than 0.3 V below the negative rail, but either may go up to +32 V whatever the supply. ESD clamps sit on the inputs and do not affect normal working.

The output swings down to the negative supply too: VOL is 5 mV typical into 10 kΩ. Outputs are short circuit protected; a short to ground may last indefinitely, typically 40 mA. A short to VCC can overheat and destroy the device, and so can shorts on both amplifiers at once.

Each amplifier has two gain stages. The input stage uses Q20 and Q18 as the differential pair, buffered by Q21 and Q17, with Q3 and Q4 converting to single-ended. That stage also shifts the level and lowers its transconductance, its pair Q20 and Q18 having split collectors, which lets a 5.0 pF compensation capacitor do the job. Its range includes the negative rail without saturating the pair or the converter. The second stage is a current-source-loaded gain stage. A bias regulator with a low temperature coefficient feeds both amplifiers, giving stable behaviour over temperature and high supply rejection.
The LM358DG/DR2G and LM2904DG/DR2G are rated 250 V HBM and 100 V MM; the other devices, including the LM2904E and LM358E, are rated 2000 V HBM and 200 V MM.
